sanskrit: sa tad ādāya mithunaṃ rājātha kṛpayānvitaḥ ājagāma gṛhān eva mama putrāv iti bruvan
english: Taking that pair, the king, filled with compassion, came home saying, "These are my children."

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃvardhayām āsa saṃskāraiś cāpy ayojayat gautamo 'pi tadāpetya dhanurvedaparo 'bhavat
english: Then he raised them and performed all their sacraments; and Gautama himself, returning at that time, became devoted to the science of archery.

sanskrit: kṛpayā yan mayā bālāv imau saṃvardhitāv iti tasmāt tayor nāma cakre tad eva sa mahīpatiḥ
english: "It is out of compassion (kṛpā) that I have raised these two children" — so saying, the king gave them that very name.

sanskrit: nihitau gautamas tatra tapasā tāv avindata āgamya cāsmai gotrādi sarvam ākhyātavāṃs tadā
english: Gautama found those two who had been abandoned there through his ascetic power, and coming to the king, he then disclosed to him their lineage and all else.

sanskrit: caturvidhaṃ dhanurvedam astrāṇi vividhāni ca nikhilenāsya tat sarvaṃ guhyam ākhyātavāṃs tadā so 'cireṇaiva kālena paramācāryatāṃ gataḥ
english: He then fully disclosed to him the fourfold science of archery and all the various weapons with their secrets; and in no great time the king attained the highest rank of mastership.

sanskrit: tato 'dhijagmuḥ sarve te dhanurvedaṃ mahārathāḥ dhṛtarāṣṭrātmajāś caiva pāṇḍavāś ca mahābalāḥ vṛṣṇayaś ca nṛpāś cānye nānādeśasamāgatāḥ
english: Thereafter all those great warriors came to study the science of archery — the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the mighty Pāṇḍavas, the Vṛṣṇis, and other kings assembled from many regions.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca viśeṣārthī tato bhīṣmaḥ pautrāṇāṃ vinayepsayā iṣvastrajñān paryapṛcchad ācāryān vīryasaṃmatān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Bhīṣma, desiring excellence for his grandsons and wishing them to be disciplined, inquired after teachers well-versed in archery and respected for their valour.

sanskrit: nālpadhīr nāmahābhāgas tathānānāstrakovidaḥ nādevasattvo vinayet kurūn astre mahābalān
english: One of small intellect, or of no great good fortune, or not versed in the many weapons, or not equal to the gods — such a one could not train the mighty Kurus in the art of arms.

sanskrit: maharṣis tu bharadvājo havirdhāne caran purā dadarśāpsarasaṃ sākṣād ghṛtācīm āplutām ṛṣiḥ
english: Now the great sage Bharadvāja, wandering long ago at the sacrificial fire-hall, beheld with his own eyes the apsarā Ghṛtācī bathing.

sanskrit: tasyā vāyuḥ samuddhūto vasanaṃ vyapakarṣata tato 'sya retaś caskanda tad ṛṣir droṇa ādadhe
english: A gust of wind swept away her garment; thereupon his seed fell, and the sage received it in a vessel called droṇa.

sanskrit: tasmin samabhavad droṇaḥ kalaśe tasya dhīmataḥ adhyagīṣṭa sa vedāṃś ca vedāṅgāni ca sarvaśaḥ
english: In that vessel was born Droṇa, the son of that wise sage; and he studied the Vedas and all the Vedic ancillary sciences fully.

sanskrit: agniveśyaṃ mahābhāgaṃ bharadvājaḥ pratāpavān pratyapādayad āgneyam astraṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: The glorious and mighty Bharadvāja, best of those who uphold dharma, taught the highly blessed Agniveśya the Āgneya weapon.

sanskrit: agniṣṭuj jātaḥ sa munis tato bharatasattama bhāradvājaṃ tadāgneyaṃ mahāstraṃ pratyapādayat
english: That sage, born of Agniṣṭut, O best of the Bharatas, then in turn transmitted that great Āgneya weapon of Bharadvāja's line to Droṇa.

sanskrit: bharadvājasakhā cāsīt pṛṣato nāma pārthivaḥ tasyāpi drupado nāma tadā samabhavat sutaḥ
english: There was a king named Pṛṣata who was a friend of Bharadvāja; his son was then born, named Drupada.

sanskrit: sa nityam āśramaṃ gatvā droṇena saha pārṣataḥ cikrīḍādhyayanaṃ caiva cakāra kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ
english: That son of Pṛṣata, bull among kṣatriyas, used to go regularly to the hermitage and played and studied there together with Droṇa.

sanskrit: tato vyatīte pṛṣate sa rājā drupado 'bhavat pāñcāleṣu mahābāhur uttareṣu nareśvaraḥ
english: Then, upon Pṛṣata's death, that long-armed man, Drupada, became king and lord of the Pāñcālas of the northern region.

sanskrit: bharadvājo 'pi bhagavān āruroha divaṃ tadā tataḥ pitṛniyuktātmā putralobhān mahāyaśāḥ śāradvatīṃ tato droṇaḥ kṛpīṃ bhāryām avindata
english: The blessed Bharadvāja too ascended to heaven at that time; then Droṇa, of great renown, his mind directed by his father's wishes and longing for a son, found Kṛpī, daughter of Śaradvan, as his wife.

sanskrit: agnihotre ca dharme ca dame ca satataṃ ratā alabhad gautamī putram aśvatthāmānam eva ca
english: She who was ever devoted to the sacred fire, to dharma, and to self-restraint — Gautamī — gave birth to a son named Aśvatthāman.

sanskrit: sa jātamātro vyanadad yathaivoccaiḥśravā hayaḥ tac chrutvāntarhitaṃ bhūtam antarikṣastham abravīt
english: The moment he was born he neighed just like the horse Uccaiḥśravas; hearing that, an invisible being standing in the sky spoke.

sanskrit: aśvasyevāsya yat sthāma nadataḥ pradiśo gatam aśvatthāmaiva bālo 'yaṃ tasmān nāmnā bhaviṣyati
english: "The sound of this boy crying has spread in all directions like the neighing of a horse (aśva); therefore this child shall bear the name Aśvatthāman."

sanskrit: sutena tena suprīto bhāradvājas tato 'bhavat tatraiva ca vasan dhīmān dhanurvedaparo 'bhavat
english: Bharadvāja's son was greatly delighted with that son; and the wise man, dwelling there, became profoundly versed in the science of archery.

sanskrit: sa śuśrāva mahātmānaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ paraṃtapam brāhmaṇebhyas tadā rājan ditsantaṃ vasu sarvaśaḥ
english: He then heard, O king, that the great-souled Jāmadagnya, the scorcher of foes, was at that time distributing all his wealth to the brahmins.

sanskrit: vanaṃ tu prasthitaṃ rāmaṃ bhāradvājas tadābravīt āgataṃ vittakāmaṃ māṃ viddhi droṇaṃ dvijarṣabham
english: As Rāma was setting out for the forest, Bharadvāja's son Droṇa addressed him: "Know that I, Droṇa, best of twice-born, have come desiring wealth."

sanskrit: rāma uvāca hiraṇyaṃ mama yac cānyad vasu kiṃ cana vidyate brāhmaṇebhyo mayā dattaṃ sarvam eva tapodhana
english: Rāma said: Whatever gold and other wealth I possessed has all been given away to the brahmins, O ascetic.

sanskrit: tathaiveyaṃ dharā devī sāgarāntā sapattanā kaśyapāya mayā dattā kṛtsnā nagaramālinī
english: Likewise this goddess Earth, bounded by the oceans, adorned with cities and towns in her entirety, has been given by me to Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: śarīramātram evādya mayedam avaśeṣitam astrāṇi ca mahārhāṇi śastrāṇi vividhāni ca vṛṇīṣva kiṃ prayacchāmi tubhyaṃ droṇa vadāśu tat
english: Only my body remains to me now, and my precious weapons and various arms. Choose — what shall I give you, Droṇa? Tell me quickly.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca astrāṇi me samagrāṇi sasaṃhārāṇi bhārgava saprayogarahasyāni dātum arhasy aśeṣataḥ
english: Droṇa said: You should give me all the weapons in their entirety, O Bhārgava, together with the means of recalling them and their applications and secrets, withholding nothing.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathety uktvā tatas tasmai prādād astrāṇi bhārgavaḥ sarahasyavrataṃ caiva dhanurvedam aśeṣataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Saying "So be it," the Bhārgava then gave him all the weapons along with their secret rites and the entire science of archery.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu tat sarvaṃ kṛtāstro dvijasattamaḥ priyaṃ sakhāyaṃ suprīto jagāma drupadaṃ prati
english: Having received all of this, that best of twice-born, now accomplished in the use of weapons, set out with great joy toward his dear friend Drupada.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato drupadam āsādya bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān abravīt pārṣataṃ rājan sakhāyaṃ viddhi mām iti
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Droṇa, the mighty son of Bharadvāja, approached Drupada and said to that son of Pṛṣata: "Know me as your friend, O king."

sanskrit: drupada uvāca akṛteyaṃ tava prajñā brahman nātisamañjasī yan māṃ bravīṣi prasabhaṃ sakhā te 'ham iti dvija
english: Drupada said: This reasoning of yours is ill-conceived, O brahmin, not well-founded — that you say to me boldly, "I am your friend," O twice-born.

sanskrit: na hi rājñām udīrṇānām evaṃ bhūtair naraiḥ kva cit sakhyaṃ bhavati mandātmañ śriyā hīnair dhanacyutaiḥ
english: With men of your condition — bereft of royal splendour and fallen from wealth — exalted kings never anywhere form friendships, O slow-witted one.

sanskrit: sauhṛdāny api jīryante kālena parijīryatām sauhṛdaṃ me tvayā hy āsīt pūrvaṃ sāmarthyabandhanam
english: Even bonds of affection decay in time as all things decay; the friendship you and I had before was based on the equality of our circumstances.

sanskrit: na sakhyam ajaraṃ loke jātu dṛśyeta karhi cit kāmo vainaṃ viharati krodhaś cainaṃ pravṛścati
english: Friendship that does not age is never to be seen anywhere in the world; desire destroys it and anger tears it asunder.

sanskrit: maivaṃ jīrṇam upāsiṣṭhāḥ sakhyaṃ navam upākuru āsīt sakhyaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha tvayā me 'rthanibandhanam
english: Do not come here clinging to that old friendship; seek a new one. The friendship between you and me, O best of twice-born, was grounded in our equal standing.

sanskrit: na daridro vasumato nāvidvān viduṣaḥ sakhā śūrasya na sakhā klībaḥ sakhipūrvaṃ kim iṣyate
english: A poor man is not the friend of a wealthy one; the ignorant man is not the friend of the learned; a coward is not the friend of a hero. What is mere former friendship worth?

sanskrit: yayor eva samaṃ vittaṃ yayor eva samaṃ kulam tayoḥ sakhyaṃ vivāhaś ca na tu puṣṭavipuṣṭayoḥ
english: Friendship and marriage exist between those of equal wealth and equal lineage, not between the prosperous and the destitute.

sanskrit: nāśrotriyaḥ śrotriyasya nārathī rathinaḥ sakhā nārājñā saṃgataṃ rājñaḥ sakhipūrvaṃ kim iṣyate
english: One ignorant of the Vedas is not the friend of a Vedic scholar; a man without a chariot is not the friend of a chariot-warrior; one who is not a king is not the equal companion of a king. What is past friendship worth?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca drupadenaivam uktas tu bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān muhūrtaṃ cintayām āsa manyunābhipariplutaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Drupada, the mighty Bharadvāja's son reflected for a moment, overwhelmed with anger.

sanskrit: sa viniścitya manasā pāñcālaṃ prati buddhimān jagāma kurumukhyānāṃ nagaraṃ nāgasāhvayam
english: Having resolved in his mind regarding Pāñcāla, that wise man went to the city of the foremost Kurus, the city named Nāgasāhvaya (Hāstinapura).

sanskrit: kumārās tv atha niṣkramya sametā gajasāhvayāt krīḍanto vīṭayā tatra vīrāḥ paryacaran mudā
english: Then the princes, having gone out together from Gajasāhvaya, were joyfully roaming about there, those heroes playing with a ball.

sanskrit: papāta kūpe sā vīṭā teṣāṃ vai krīḍatāṃ tadā na ca te pratyapadyanta karma vīṭopalabdhaye
english: As they played, that ball fell into a well, and they could find no means to recover the ball.

sanskrit: atha droṇaḥ kumārāṃs tān dṛṣṭvā kṛtyavatas tadā prahasya mandaṃ paiśalyād abhyabhāṣata vīryavān
english: Then Droṇa, seeing those princes at a loss, smiled gently and spoke to them out of his skill and confidence.

sanskrit: aho nu dhig balaṃ kṣātraṃ dhig etāṃ vaḥ kṛtāstratām bharatasyānvaye jātā ye vīṭāṃ nādhigacchata
english: "Shame on kṣatriya strength! Shame on your claimed training in arms — born in the lineage of Bharata, yet you cannot retrieve a ball!"

sanskrit: eṣa muṣṭir iṣīkāṇāṃ mayāstreṇābhimantritaḥ asya vīryaṃ nirīkṣadhvaṃ yad anyasya na vidyate
english: "Here is a handful of reeds consecrated by me with a weapon-spell; observe the power of this which no other possesses."

sanskrit: vetsyāmīṣīkayā vīṭāṃ tām iṣīkām athānyayā tām anyayā samāyogo vīṭāyā grahaṇe mama
english: "I shall pierce the ball with one reed, then that reed with another, and by joining them together I shall retrieve the ball — that is my method."

sanskrit: tad apaśyan kumārās te vismayotphullalocanāh aveṣkya coddhṛtāṃ vīṭāṃ vīṭāveddhāram abruvan
english: The princes watched this with eyes wide with amazement; and having seen the ball retrieved, they addressed the one who had pierced it.

sanskrit: abhivādayāmahe brahman naitad anyeṣu vidyate ko 'si kaṃ tvābhijānīmo vayaṃ kiṃ karavāmahe
english: "We bow to you, O brahmin! This skill is found in no other. Who are you? How shall we know you? And what shall we do for you?"

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca ācakṣadhvaṃ ca bhīṣmāya rūpeṇa ca guṇaiś ca mām sa eva sumahābuddhiḥ sāṃprataṃ pratipatsyate
english: Droṇa said: Describe me to Bhīṣma by my appearance and my qualities; he alone, of great intelligence, will understand at once who I am.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathety uktvā tu te sarve bhīṣmam ūcuḥ pitāmaham brāhmaṇasya vacas tathyaṃ tac ca karmaviśeṣavat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Saying "So be it," they all went to their grandfather Bhīṣma and reported the brahmin's words along with that remarkable deed.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaḥ śrutvā kumārāṇāṃ droṇaṃ taṃ pratyajānata yuktarūpaḥ sa hi gurur ity evam anucintya ca
english: Bhīṣma, hearing the princes' account, recognized that it was Droṇa, reflecting: "He is indeed the fitting teacher."

sanskrit: athainam ānīya tadā svayam eva susatkṛtam paripapraccha nipuṇaṃ bhīṣmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ hetum āgamane tasya droṇaḥ sarvaṃ nyavedayat
english: Then Bhīṣma, best of weapon-bearers, having brought him and honoured him well himself, questioned him carefully about his purpose in coming; and Droṇa disclosed everything.

sanskrit: maharṣer agniveśyasya sakāśam aham acyuta astrārtham agamaṃ pūrvaṃ dhanurvedajighṛkṣayā
english: "O Acyuta, I formerly went to the great sage Agniveśya desiring to acquire weapons and wishing to master the science of archery."

sanskrit: brahmacārī vinītātmā jaṭilo bahulāḥ samāḥ avasaṃ tatra suciraṃ dhanurvedacikīrṣayā
english: "As a celibate student, with controlled mind, with matted hair, I dwelt there for many years with the desire to master the science of archery."

sanskrit: pāñcālarājaputras tu yajñaseno mahābalaḥ mayā sahākarod vidyāṃ guroḥ śrāmyan samāhitaḥ
english: "The mighty prince of the Pāñcālas, Yajñasena's son, also studied the same learning under the same teacher alongside me, striving and concentrated."

sanskrit: sa me tatra sakhā cāsīd upakārī priyaś ca me tenāhaṃ saha saṃgamya ratavān suciraṃ bata bālyāt prabhṛti kauravya sahādhyayanam eva ca
english: "He was my friend there, helpful and dear to me; delighting long in his company, O descendant of Kuru, we had been studying together from childhood indeed."

sanskrit: sa samāsādya māṃ tatra priyakārī priyaṃvadaḥ abravīd iti māṃ bhīṣma vacanaṃ prītivardhanam
english: "That one, kind in deed and kind in word, approached me there and said to me, O Bhīṣma, words that increased my joy."

sanskrit: ahaṃ priyatamaḥ putraḥ pitur droṇa mahātmanaḥ abhiṣekṣyati māṃ rājye sa pāñcālyo yadā tadā
english: "'I am the dearest son to my great-souled father, O Droṇa; when that Pāñcāla king consecrates me in his kingdom —'"

sanskrit: tvadbhojyaṃ bhavitā rājyaṃ sakhe satyena te śape mama bhogāś ca vittaṃ ca tvadadhīnaṃ sukhāni ca
english: "'— the kingdom shall be yours to enjoy, my friend; I swear it to you by truth: my pleasures, my wealth, and my happiness shall all be at your disposal.'"

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pravavrāja kṛtāstro 'haṃ dhanepsayā abhiṣiktaṃ ca śrutvainaṃ kṛtārtho 'smīti cintayan
english: "Thus assured, I set forth, having mastered the weapons, desirous of wealth; and hearing that he had been consecrated, I thought: 'My purpose is achieved.'"

sanskrit: priyaṃ sakhāyaṃ suprīto rājyasthaṃ punar āvrajam saṃsmaran saṃgamaṃ caiva vacanaṃ caiva tasya tat
english: "Full of joy, I came again to my dear friend who now held a kingdom, remembering our fellowship and those very words of his."

sanskrit: tato drupadam āgamya sakhipūrvam ahaṃ prabho abruvaṃ puruṣavyāghra sakhāyaṃ viddhi mām iti
english: "Then, approaching Drupada and invoking our old friendship, I said to him, O lord, O tiger among men: 'Know me as your friend.'"

sanskrit: upasthitaṃ tu drupadaḥ sakhivac cābhisaṃgatam sa māṃ nirākāram iva prahasann idam abravīt
english: "But Drupada, though I had come to him as a friend and greeted him as one, seemed to dismiss me and laughingly said this:"

sanskrit: akṛteyaṃ tava prajñā brahman nātisamañjasī yad āttha māṃ tvaṃ prasabhaṃ sakhā te 'ham iti dvija
english: "'This thinking of yours is ill-formed, O brahmin, not well-founded — that you say to me boldly, "I am your friend," O twice-born.'"

sanskrit: na hi rājñām udīrṇānām evaṃbhūtair naraiḥ kva cit sakhyaṃ bhavati mandātmañ śriyā hīnair dhanacyutaiḥ
english: "'Exalted kings never form friendships anywhere with men of your condition — bereft of royal splendour, fallen from wealth, O slow-witted one.'"

sanskrit: nāśrotriyaḥ śrotriyasya nārathī rathinaḥ sakhā nārājā pārthivasyāpi sakhipūrvaṃ kim iṣyate
english: "'One ignorant of the Vedas is not the friend of a Vedic scholar; one without a chariot is not the friend of a chariot-warrior; a non-king is not the friend of a king. What is past friendship worth?'"

sanskrit: drupadenaivam ukto 'haṃ manyunābhipariplutaḥ abhyāgacchaṃ kurūn bhīṣma śiṣyair arthī guṇānvitaiḥ
english: "Thus addressed by Drupada, overwhelmed with anger, I have come to the Kurus, O Bhīṣma, seeking worthy students endowed with noble qualities."

sanskrit: pratijagrāha taṃ bhīṣmo guruṃ pāṇḍusutaiḥ saha pautrān ādāya tān sarvān vasūni vividhāni ca
english: Bhīṣma accepted that teacher along with the sons of Pāṇḍu, bringing all his grandsons together with various precious gifts.

sanskrit: śiṣyā iti dadau rājan droṇāya vidhipūrvakam sa ca śiṣyān maheṣvāsaḥ pratijagrāha kauravān
english: He gave them as pupils to Droṇa according to proper rites, O king; and that great archer accepted the Kauravas as his students.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tān sarvān droṇo vacanam abravīt rahasy ekaḥ pratītātmā kṛtopasadanāṃs tadā
english: Having accepted all of them, Droṇa spoke privately, alone, to those who had duly performed the rite of approaching a teacher, his heart at ease.

sanskrit: kāryaṃ me kāṅkṣitaṃ kiṃ cid dhṛdi saṃparivartate kṛtāstrais tat pradeyaṃ me tad ṛtaṃ vadatānaghāḥ
english: "There is a certain desired task that revolves in my heart; once you are accomplished in weapons, it must be rendered to me — speak truth about that, O sinless ones."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā kauraveyās te tūṣṇīm āsan viśāṃ pate arjunas tu tataḥ sarvaṃ pratijajñe paraṃtapaḥ
english: Hearing this, the descendants of Kuru fell silent, O lord of people; but Arjuna, the scorcher of foes, then pledged to do everything.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaṃ mūrdhni tadā samāghrāya punaḥ punaḥ prītipūrvaṃ pariṣvajya praruroda mudā tadā
english: Then Droṇa smelled Arjuna's head again and again, embraced him with affection, and wept with joy.

sanskrit: tato droṇaḥ pāṇḍuputrān astrāṇi vividhāni ca grāhayām āsa divyāni mānuṣāṇi ca vīryavān
english: Then mighty Droṇa proceeded to instruct the sons of Pāṇḍu in all the various weapons — both divine and human.

sanskrit: rājaputrās tathaivānye sametya bharatarṣabha abhijagmus tato droṇam astrārthe dvijasattamam vṛṣṇayaś cāndhakāś caiva nānādeśyāś ca pārthivāḥ
english: Other princes likewise came together, O bull of the Bharatas, and approached that best of twice-born, Droṇa, for instruction in weapons — the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas and kings from many lands.

sanskrit: sūtaputraś ca rādheyo guruṃ droṇam iyāt tadā spardhamānas tu pārthena sūtaputro 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ duryodhanam upāśritya pāṇḍavān atyamanyata
english: And the son of the sūta, Rādheya, also came to the teacher Droṇa at that time; but that son of a sūta, extremely intolerant, rivalling Pārtha, took shelter with Duryodhana and held the Pāṇḍavas in contempt.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca arjunas tu paraṃ yatnam ātasthe gurupūjane astre ca paramaṃ yogaṃ priyo droṇasya cābhavat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But Arjuna exerted the utmost effort in revering the teacher and applied himself supremely to the weapons; he became the beloved of Droṇa.

sanskrit: droṇena tu tadāhūya rahasy ukto 'nnasādhakaḥ andhakāre 'rjunāyānnaṃ na deyaṃ te kathaṃ cana
english: Droṇa summoned the one who prepared food and said to him privately: "You are never, under any circumstances, to serve food to Arjuna in the dark."

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid bhuñjāne pravavau vāyur arjune tena tatra pradīpaḥ sa dīpyamāno nivāpitaḥ
english: Then one day while Arjuna was eating, the wind blew and the burning lamp was extinguished by it.

sanskrit: bhuṅkta evārjuno bhaktaṃ na cāsyāsyād vyamuhyata hastas tejasvino nityam annagrahaṇakāraṇāt tad abhyāsakṛtaṃ matvā rātrāv abhyasta pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Yet Arjuna went on eating his food; his glorious hand did not falter, always finding the food by force of habit. Recognizing this as the product of constant practice, the son of Pāṇḍu then practised archery by night.
